quest.title: An Overnight Fantasyland
quest.description: Out of a mixture of curiosity and concern, you and Paimon head back to the Court of Fontaine for a stroll around.
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

talks.objective: Go to the newsstand in the Court of Fontaine

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, there's a newsstand over there. Wanna grab a copy of The Steambird?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We know our Fontainian friends love a little drama — there's no way they'd let their readers down!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, isn't that Charlotte? And standing next to her, surely that can't be... Kinich!?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Hmm, how about... "Lost Treasure Resurfaces At Last! Behold the Beauty of the Remurian Teacup."

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Hmm... Hold up, this one's a gem: "Illegal Restaurant Caught Serving Saurian Stew — Proves Surprisingly Popular."

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Huh, pretty shocking. But it still feels like it's... missing something. Ah, got it:

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: "Iudex Gravely Wounded in Shocking Stabbing, Set to Miss Cross-Border Smuggling Trial!"

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: My oh my, that can't be for real...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Ugh, fine. I hate to admit it, but you've won this one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Huh? What!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did Paimon hear that right? Neuvillette was... stabbed? And... gravely wounded!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, surely that can't be right... Can it?

choices.text: Surely not.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: #Aha, I thought I heard familiar voices! Well, if it isn't {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: What a coincidence! Mr. Kinich and I were talking about you two just a few minutes ago!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Unfortunately for me, he's a very loyal friend — I pressed him for some juicy details, but he remained tight-lipped about you.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: #So, uh... Anything you wanna share with me about the great {NICKNAME}'s triumphant exploits in Natlan...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ahem... It was a team effort.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: *sigh* Modest as ever...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Anyway, I'm getting a bit ahead of myself. Sorry!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Lemme backtrack a little — Hi you two! It's been ages! What brings you back to Fontaine?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Hey there, you two. Fancy running into you here.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What a pleasant surprise!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that... and also a less-than-pleasant shock!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What the heck was all that about a Saurian meat restaurant and the Iudex getting stabbed? Please say you weren't being serious...?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Ohhh, that? We were just trading tabloid headlines, is that what you're talking about?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Trading tabloid headlines?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Yeah. Charlotte and I were having a little contest to see who could find the most ridiculous fake news stories.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Either I got lucky, or I have a knack for honing in on the most outrageous material.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: *sigh* I'm sorry you had to see such an unflattering side to Fontaine, Mr. Kinich.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: These third-rate tabloids write their headlines purely to shock and scandalize. All they care about is grabbing your attention to boost their sales.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: The ones who've still got a shred of integrity will at least clarify the truth in the main body of the article — although the misleading headline is still an underhanded trick to draw readers in.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: But others, like the one we were just reading aloud, have no qualms about making outright fabrications.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: If I had to quantify it, I'd say about one percent of what they write is the truth.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: That's pretty lenient of you, Mr. Kinich.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Huh!? Him? Lenient? You've gotta be kid— Uhh!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to give credit to these so-called "news" stories for occasionally including a grain of truth. All I'm saying is, even the wildest leaps of the human imagination are always rooted in reality.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean, all those fake headlines you mentioned actually do have some basis in fact?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Sure they do. For instance, there was, in fact, a smuggling trial recently.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Considering the amount of speculation surrounding the smuggled goods, it's no wonder there are rumors about restaurants serving Saurian meat or teacups being unearthed from ancient ruins.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: But in reality, the goods in question were simply a few ancient relics dug up from ruins in Natlan.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Rest assured — no Saurians were harmed in the process.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: And, if you're wondering why the Iudex didn't preside over the trial, it's because this case was assigned to another judge right from the offset.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: It's not as if the Palais Mermonia only has one judge. We can't expect Monsieur Neuvillette to handle every single case himself.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: On a more interesting note... the trial in question went remarkably smoothly, and it was all thanks to Mr. Kinich's testimony as a key witness.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, okay! Hehe, Paimon was so busy freaking out about those headlines that she totally forgot to ask why you're here in Fontaine, Kinich!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Phew, it was all a misunderstanding. The world's not going to end!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: *sigh* Maybe not, but it'd be an even better world for me if Mr. Kinich here would agree to another exclusive interview with The Steambird...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: It was a pretty open-and-shut case, and my testimony in court was clear enough.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: But I'm guessing, Mademoiselle Charlotte, that you're less interested in the case than you are in trying to uncover some news stories about Natlan.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Drat, you saw right through me... Guess I'll put it down to the keen instincts of a renowned Saurian-hunter. Any response to that, or...?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I appreciate your kind invitation, but like I said, storytelling isn't really my forte...

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Hahahahaha! Kinich the Speechless! Kinich the Tongue-Tied!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: #...If you're dead-set on doing an interview, why not talk to {NICKNAME} instead?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Back to me again?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Ah, of course! That's a brilliant idea!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: But that also means I'll need a bit more time to prep. Let me put together a thorough list of interview questions!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like I'm not allowed to refuse?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Hehe, well, I know I can be persistent, but at the end of the day, it's your call.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Anyway, I should probably be getting back to work. I also need to go track down a Gestionnaire and report these increasingly outrageous tabloids!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Farewell, my friends! Until we meet again!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Charlotte never stops, does she...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Um, anyway, Paimon just has to ask...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That... Ajaw-thing that popped out before — or was it Ajaw? It kinda looked like Ajaw, but at the same time...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Oh, that thing.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Yeah, that was Ajaw.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's up with him? Like, he's still noisy, but he's waaay quieter than before — it's like he's trying to hide, or something.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe he's not acclimatizing very well to Fontaine?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Could be.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not acclimatizing? Hah! Aw, poor Almighty Dragonlord is not feeling well!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: ...Too bad he can't come out to argue back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... What do you mean?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: There's nothing "physically" wrong with him. It actually has to do with a strange law we learned about after arriving in Fontaine.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Apparently, it's forbidden to release flying objects within Fontaine city limits during the first three days of each month.

choices.text: Oh, I get it now!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon sure does!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's been down this road before, there's an easy solution! As long as Kinich holds onto Ajaw's tail, he'll be considered an "Almighty Dragonlord Balloon," not a "Flying Almighty Dragonlord."

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Not gonna lie, I was considering that. But Ajaw wasn't too thrilled with the idea of huffing and puffing away in the form of a mini helium balloon.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: That said, it's pretty annoying how he keeps randomly popping up all of a sudden.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Anyway, this morning, I saw a notice outside the Palais Mermonia about an event that's set to take place outside the city soon. Something to do with filmmaking. I hear that's all the rage here.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I was planning to stay here and do some exploring for a few extra days anyway, so I think I'll go check it out.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: It'll be a good chance to let that noisy helium balloon out — he might even learn a thing or two.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: If you're free, why don't you come along?

choices.text: Sure, seeing Ajaw angry always makes my day.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I know where it is, so let me lead the way.

choices.text: Sure, always up for a bit of fun!
And I'm sure Paimon gets it even better!
If it is, we're all toast.

talks.objective: Say hi to your old friends
Take a stroll outside the city with Kinich

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Looks like I remembered correctly — here we are.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, this is awesome! Hard to believe it was just an empty beach before.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Yeah. It was still completely deserted only a few days ago when I passed by on my way to testify at the opera house.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: There must be some efficient workers in Fontaine. Quite impressive.
A few days? One night was all it took! Rap-a-tap-tap... Ta-da!
But... Is this all it takes to blow people away? ...No, no, no, given my past experience, I can't let myself get carried away...

choices.text: There's something oddly familiar about the way you talk...

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Wow, I can't believe you actually remember me! It's me, Lepine-Pauline — that's right, the unlucky one!

choices.text: Good to see you again! The prototype lens has come in handy, by the way.

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Of course! How else would we have managed to build Fantasyland in a single night?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Fantasyland?

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: At least, that's how I like to think of it myself — a magical land of fantasy, the stuff of film buffs' dreams!

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: I know it sounds like I'm laying it on thick, but that really is the goal here.

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: As you can see, the theme of this amusement park is Fontainian film-making, a place for all film lovers to come together and co-construct a world of dreams!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Co-construct? Well, that's a relief. Sounds like you're sharing the costs this time, rather than pouring your entire life savings into a single project.

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Nope! I might be inviting others to help fund this, but that doesn't mean I haven't thrown all my life savings into it too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? You've gotta be kidding!

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Ha! Look at you, puny little humans... Recklessly betting your entire future against some stupid vanity project!

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: If you're expecting even an ounce of sympathy from the Almighty Dragonlord, dream on! Mockery is all you shall get, straight from the heart!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Sorry, just ignore that little gizmoid — he likes to butt in occasionally. Do go on.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: "Gizmoid"? Who are you calling gizmoid!? YOU'RE the gizmoid!!!

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Wow, that's quite a nifty meka you've got yourself there! Is it some sort of smart personal assistant?

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: You ought to let Miss Charlotte see your cool gadget — who knows, maybe you could even look into mass-production!

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Mass production!? Ugh, insolent, vulgar, and disrespectful!

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: I, the Almighty Dragonlord, am one of a kind! There has never been another like me, nor will there ever be!

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: And another thing — "smart" is the understatement of the century!

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: I shall have you know that I am K'uhul Ajaw, forebear of ancient wisdom! I lived for eons long before any of you were born!

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Wh—What!? Heavens above, I beg your pardon, forebear of ancient wisdom! Please, I meant no offense!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Idiot meets idiot...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Haha, what's all the fuss? Making some new friends, are we?

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Miss Navia!

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Allow me to introduce the star behind all the work that's gone into this venue — Miss Navia, President of Fontaine's Spina di Rosula!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hello, everyone! Partner, Paimon, how have you been lately?

choices.text: Ah, my trusty partner!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Hello there, I'm Kinich.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: ...What about me, what about ME? My useless servant can't even give me a proper introduction...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: You think someone yelling their name out in the middle of a public street really needs an introduction?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hahaha, he's not wrong! I caught yours just now, in fact.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: So, you must be the Almighty Dragonlord, Mr. Ajaw. It's a pleasure to meet you.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: See that? That's what I call proper manners!

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Well, well, it's not every day you meet a well-mannered human. Navia, was it? Excellent. You may address the Almighty Dragonlord by his name!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Umm, Navia, don't you think the title "Almighty Dragonlord" is a bit... silly? Hehe...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It's no big deal! All little animals do that, don't they? I mean, try to puff themselves up to look more impressive?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ajaw's totally being treated like a little cuddly pet...

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Anyway, it's all thanks to Miss Navia and the Spina di Rosula that Fantasyland's gotten up and running in the space of a single night.

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Ah, honestly, thank heavens! After all that paperwork and endless waiting, the event and venue finally got the green light... *sobs*

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: I couldn't wait a moment longer! The second the approval came through, I reached out to President Navia, hoping she could lend a hand.

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: After all, who else but the Spina di Rosula would indulge such impulsive demands... *sobs*

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: #Sorry, {NICKNAME}. Miss Lepine-Pauline sometimes gets a bit overwhelmed by her own excitement, as you can see...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I'm guessing she hasn't gone into much detail about the event yet, so let me fill you in.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: In short, the Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland is a fan convention that's open to film enthusiasts from all over Teyvat. Miss Lepine-Pauline is hosting this event and also providing technical support.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Chevalmarin?

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: That's right, the one and only Surintendante Chevalmarin!

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: After much persistence and many solicitations, I finally obtained Lady Furina's permission to use the image of her close friend.

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Not only is our adorable mascot drawing in fans by the minute, but she's also boosting her own popularity — and that was always the goal, a win-win arrangement!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's been a while since we last met, but still, it's a surprise to hear Lepine-Pauline coming out with such... sensible ideas...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way, Miss Lepine-Pauline, have you decided to switch careers and go into film tech?

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Mm, not exactly. By chance, one of the prototype lenses I developed caught a photographer's eye, and it's now being used for the latest cinematic productions.

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Thanks to this unexpected opportunity, I've had the chance to invent various film-related equipment and props.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That's right, so don't underestimate Miss Lepine-Pauline, our resident engineer! She's the technical powerhouse at the core of this entire event.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: As for the Spina di Rosula, we're mainly here to take care of planning, operations, and management.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: For anyone feeling inspired to set up a booth, Miss Lepine-Pauline and I will provide the necessary technical and operational support once their application has been approved.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: #By the way, {NICKNAME}, are you at all interested in taking part?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It would be a chance for you to earn some extra income. Plus, with your skills, I'm sure you could bring something special to the table!

choices.text: Sounds like a lot of fun.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon would be even more tempted if you were to, say, throw in one of those fancy feasts she's seen in those gourmet food reels!

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Well, as it happens, that'll be a piece of cake!

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Everyone needs to eat, whether they be tourists or the stall owners themselves.

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: So, thanks to Miss Navia's help, we've managed to invite none other than the celebrity chef Miss Escoffier to run our theme restaurant!

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Look, over th—

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: You, yes, YOU! For the last time, the ingredients have to be in the right ratio! Get it right next time, or you might as well just lie down on the chopping board yourself!

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: ...Haha, she seems a bit busy right now...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Well, I'm sold. I think I'll make Ajaw go be her assistant.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: You little... What's your game here?

response.speaker: Spina di Rosula Member
response.text: Demoiselle, sorry to bother you, but there's an issue over here that requires your personal attention!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Ah, apologies, looks like it's back to work with me. Please feel free to take a gander at what we've got.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: #Anyway, {NICKNAME}, if you're interested in taking part, come find me later.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure thing.

choices.text: I'll think about it.
Very well, thanks. Even better now that you're here.
Been keeping yourself busy with some proper work lately?
Um... Who are you again?

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Oh no, you've forgotten me... Does "Graph Adversarial Technology" ring any bells? It's me, Lepine-Pauline!

choices.text: Good to see you again! The prototype lens has come in handy, by the way.
Been keeping yourself busy with some proper work lately?

talks.objective: Find out more about the convention by asking Lepine-Pauline

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Greetings. Apologies if you overheard my harsh words just now, but I assure you it is entirely necessary.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: The sheer lack of standards here will be the death of me... Do you have any idea of the kind of customers I'm gonna get with how lax things are at the moment?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: ...The ones that leave their guns behind by accident! And then come back to collect them later, bringing ammunition with them!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's the kind of customer you wouldn't forget in a hurry...

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Ah... haha...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Wait, has that happened before?

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: No, no, it's just the mention of guns reminded me... Someone did actually leave their gun nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Just before we started setting up, as we were cleaning up the site, someone stumbled upon a mysterious locked box...

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: It didn't look like something from Fontaine, though. It had more of a... Natlanese vibe?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Oh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: D'you think a foreign tourist might have left it behind?

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: That's what I assumed at first. But the box was buried beneath a pile of wooden planks, rocks, and whatnot, so it seemed like someone deliberately hid it there.

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: But I didn't see much point in speculating, so the best thing I could think of was to hand it over to the authorities.

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: I trekked all the way over to the Palais Mermonia just to hand it in. Ugh, it was exhausting.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: What did the authorities make of it?

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Oh, they made a mountain out of a molehill. As usual.

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Before even addressing the question of what was actually inside the box, they had several heated discussions about whose responsibility it was to write the lost-and-found notice...

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Thankfully, the ever-reliable Officer Sedene stepped up and immediately called in the Marechaussee Phantom to crack the lock and check if there were any dangerous items inside.

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: And as it turned out, there was — a gun!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that's a dangerous item alright...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Mind if I ask what kind of gun it was?

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, Mr. Kinich, you're from Natlan, aren't you? Do you know a lot about guns?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: You could say it comes with the job. I have an interest in weaponry and the like.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Ugh, such a spoiled brat. What, are the toys I gave you not good enough for you anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Yep, got sick of those long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: You little...! How dare you turn your nose up at my gifts! Why, I... Mmph!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Time for a time-out, old timer.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Sorry, where were we? Oh yeah, do you recall what the gun looked like?

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Uh... It's a bit hard to describe. If you ask me, it didn't even really look like a gun...

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Oh! Give me a second, I'll knock out a quick sketch...

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Something like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it's so neat and precise!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sketched by a professional engineer, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's nothing...

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Uh, sorry... Is something wrong with my drawing...?

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: I know it doesn't really look like a gun, but I assure you, this is exactly what it looked like!

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: And it certainly could shoot as well, too — I confirmed that with the officer from the Marechaussee Phantom.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: No, no, quite the opposite. The features are very accurate — and it is definitely from Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Please, don't mind me, I'm just taking a moment to admire it.

choices.text: Thanks a lot, Lepine-Pauline.

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: I should be the one thanking you! Thank you, and everyone else, for your support!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Don't mention it. Besides, we haven't really done anything.

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Not at all! The buzz and excitement you guys bring is exactly what this event needs!

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Oh dear... I'm starting to feel a bit guilty watching everyone else toil away. Guess it's about time I got back to work too...

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: #But just before I go, one last thing! {NICKNAME}, it's wonderful to see you. Here's to a successful collaboration!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (It seems like Kinich has something to say. Let's go find a quiet spot.)

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After saying goodbye to Lepine-Pauline, you and Kinich find somewhere you can chat.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I'm sure you noticed that there was something unusual about that "gun."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It looked ancient...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Correct. It's most likely an old weapon dug up from some ancient dragon ruins.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Based on my experience, it might be more accurate to refer to it as a "hand cannon." But in Fontaine terms, it's not wrong to call it a "gun."

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Given why I came here, don't you think it's curious that an ancient dragon relic of unknown origin would turn up like this, out of the blue? I suspect this gun might have something to do with that smuggling case — it might've slipped through the cracks.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Time is of the essence, so I'd like to head over to the Palais Mermonia to verify my suspicions.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think I'll join you.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Perfect. Then we can head out right away.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Or, if you want to catch up with your friends first, I can wait.

choices.text: Can't wait for the event to get started.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Anyway, back on topic. Wait a second, I lost my train of thought... What were we talking about again?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why you're all here, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa & Ororon
dialogues.text: For Cacucu!\nFor vegetables.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I'll go first. It's for the... "Chevrolamine Film Fantasyland." ...Wait, is that right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's "Chevalmarin."

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Ah, right. I keep stumbling over that one...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Guess I owe Chevalmarin an apology, even if she's not here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's okay...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Anyway, long story short, the festival restaurant urgently needed fresh vegetables from Natlan, which is why Ifa and I are here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you guys are... vegetable couriers?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: He is. I'm just here as a responsible adult.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: It's his first time traveling so far away from home, and all the elders in his tribe were worried. So they had me come along.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Even though it's your first time too.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Right, but they still picked me to accompany you. You gotta wonder why that might be.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Don't you get it? They all just saw how overworked you were, so they used it as an excuse to send you off on a vacation.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: ...Wait, what? So I'm getting the grandson treatment now, too?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: See? Doesn't matter how much older you are than this dude. Hang out with him long enough, and you'll eventually find yourself being treated like a kid.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Meaning, everyone looks after you. What's so bad about that?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: In theory, nothing at all.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: In that case, guess I'd better start over. Hi guys, my name's Ifa, and I just turned five.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nice to meet you, lil' bro.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Paimon's not sure who the responsible adult is anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what about Cacucu?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If he was here, we'd be making more of a ruckus than we already are...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: *sigh* That's exactly what's got me worried.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Ifa, there's nothing to worry about.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: You're a big boy. You can handle yourself now, even without Cacucu.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: You think that's what I'm worried about!?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Anyway, my priority right now is Cacucu...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Suffice it to say, Cacucu's in big doo-doo.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How so? He's so small, and all he knows are a few harmless phrases... What kind of trouble could he even get himself into?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Lemme guess — did he get caught out by the law on "flying objects"?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Bro... you too?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Not me. Ajaw.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Oh, that pesky little chatterbox.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: So that's why he hasn't interrupted us this whole time... Guess he's too scared to show his face.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: That, plus he's already spouted enough nonsense for one day, so I've put him on mute until tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Nice one! If I was even half as decisive as you are, I would've kept a closer hold on Cacucu so he didn't get a chance to go flying off...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I guess that's what "flying objects" do...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, bro... Uhh, or rather... Did Cacucu get caught by the guards for flying around?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: If they'd managed that, we'd at least be able to track him down.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: But when the guards started chasing him, Cacucu flew into that building next door.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I wouldn't be surprised if there was a high-stakes pursuit going down in there as we speak, just like one of those cool crime movies.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—Which building?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...That one!?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Yup, that's the one. Cacucu sure has a good eye for a getaway — it's the tallest building around.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I may be able to fly up pretty high, but checking every last window would still take quite a while.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: As for Ifa... Well, let's just say he's not flying anywhere without a Saurian. Sorry about that.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Not like that's my fault, though. You don't have to apologize on my behalf...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a sec, what's this got to do with how high you can fly!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cacucu's got himself into a real mess here, like a panicked animal running straight into a trap. It's pretty worrying...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's starting to picture him flapping through a barrage of gunfire, while important documents are flying about left, right, and center...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Heck yeah! If anyone can pull it off, it's Cacucu — he's always been such an awesomesaurus. I believe in him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (In other words... right now, in this building, there could be not one awesomesaurus, but two...)

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: For real, now? Do you even hear yourself, bro?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Of course I'm for real. I'd never make light of something like that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, everyone's an awesomesaurus... Well, uh, the human version...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But our priority right now should be to go in there and check up on Cacucu.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: As it happens, Kinich and I were just heading over to the Palais Mermonia for something else.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Leave it to us.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: You sure? Awesome, that'll be a huge help!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: And if Cacucu doesn't listen to you, I give you permission to pull out a couple of his feathers.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Wait... Since when was that up to you?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Well, then it's your call, bro.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Alright then. If Cacucu doesn't listen to you, I also give you permission to pull out a couple of his feathers.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: There you go. If he objects to that, tell him to come find us.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Ha, he won't. Trust me.

talks.objective: Enter the Palais Mermonia to check on the situation

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: No way, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Mmm...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Did he say he came from Natlan?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette & Cacucu
dialogues.text: No.\nGet outta here!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I can understand his words, just... not what they mean.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: For real, now...

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Bro!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Haha... He keeps repeating the same things, over and over again.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Oh, you know one another?

choices.text: He's a bro.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He's a friend, yeah... A Saurian friend, let's say.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Great, well that was easy. Looks like we've tracked down the owner.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Guess that's one less lost-and-found notice for you to write, Monsieur Neuvillette...

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: For real!?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, was there something important you wanted to discuss with the Iudex?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: I'm just about done with my business here. Need me to step out?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Stay and hear them out first. Perhaps it will have some bearing on your own work.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: If I'm not mistaken, you are the same Mr. Kinich who served as a witness in the smuggling trial.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I take it there's been a further development in the case?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: That's right... Very perceptive, Mr. Iudex.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, so you've met Neuvillette before? But wasn't the trial overseen by another judge?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I've seen his photo in the papers.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: But as for this other gentleman...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Ah. Allow me to introduce you to Mr. Wriothesley, administrator of the Fortress of Meropide... Or in layman's terms, Fontaine's prison warden.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Please, feel free to share anything about the case. There's no need to keep anything from him.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Pleasure to meet you.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Pleasure to meet you!

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Wow, that sounded just like me...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: But... should we really discuss official business in front of a Saurian...?

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Oh wow, oh no!

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I believe he said...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Or rather, I suppose he meant that he'll keep this to himself.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Though I should mention, Mr. Cacucu, that we will have to ask you to sign a confidentiality agreement.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Sure thing, bro!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (This is all a bit strange, but they really are a great pair of... awesomesauri.)

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Let us return to the matter at hand.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Mr. Kinich, was there something else you wanted to discuss relating to the case?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Yes, let me fill you in...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Kinich tells Neuvillette and Wriothesley about Lepine-Pauline finding the "gun."

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Neuvillette makes inquiries with the relevant personnel, and sure enough, they locate the box and the gun that Lepine-Pauline spoke of.

choices.text: He's a bro of a bro.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He's a friend, yeah... A Saurian friend of a human friend.

talks.objective: Tell Ororon and Ifa about what's been going on

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ororon, Ifa! We found Cacucu!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: What's the situation? How bad is it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's some good news and some bad news.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Oh no...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: When I saw that Cacucu wasn't with you, I'd already prepared myself for the worst...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Relax, Ifa. Maybe Cacucu just prefers high-rise living now.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Sometimes, you just have to let the kids grow up and make their own choices in life.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: ...For real, now? Do you even hear yourself, bro?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's not that bad!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cacucu's fine! Still very much alive and kicking, for starters.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: He hasn't been arrested either, so no jail time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Even had an interesting chat with some veritable VIPs.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: See?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: You're not exactly reassuring me here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: As for the bad news... Well, it's really not that bad!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cacucu accidentally overheard some top-secret stuff, so he has to stay at the Palais Mermonia for a while to sign a confidentiality agreement.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But there's no need to worry! The person in charge of looking after Cacucu is super nice, so he'll be absolutely fine.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You'll just have to wait a bit longer.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Phew... Alright, that doesn't sound too bad after all! Wow, hearing that's put my mind to rest.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: But based on my understanding of how things work here, the ban on flying objects should be over by the time Cacucu actually gets out.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: What a shame. Oh well, I guess we'll just have to go have some fun without him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You don't look disappointed in the slightest!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Anyway, Ororon and I will be staying in guest rooms upstairs at the Hotel Debord for the time being. Feel free to drop by if you need us.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright, bro.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay, problem solved! Alright, let's catch up another day!

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: We've gone over budget in quite a few areas, but... Ah, whatever! The results are what count!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I know you mentioned a while back that people from Natlan would soon start showing up all over the world, but I hadn't expected anything like this.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: It seems no matter where they come from, all dragons are inquisitive by nature...

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: You can say that again, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The same might well be said for humankind.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The real reason you chose to stay to investigate this case was your curiosity about Natlan and Mr. Cacucu, was it not?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Haha, guilty as charged. Nothing gets past you.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: So, how about we take this opportunity to chat a little more? We've got the world's best translator on hand, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Sure thing, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Oh, man...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Bro!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Are you mimicking me? Now's not the time, c'mon...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: No, I mean... One of our buddies is here, for real. Quite a few of them, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ororon! What are you doing here? And who's this...?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Allow me to introduce you.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Bro, meet bro.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Which bro we talkin' about?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: A bro who heals other bros.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Ah, that bro. Nice to meet you, bro.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: You guys...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, please... If Paimon hears the word "bro" one more time...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I'm so sorry, Paimon. I had no idea you were allergic to bro talk...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Quick, Ifa, Paimon needs medical intervention.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Seriously, br... I mean, dude, sometimes I honestly can't tell if you're being serious or just messing around.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: And Kinich, come on, br... other. We've known each other for how long now, and even you won't let me off the hook?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: It's quite hard to resist.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: #*sigh* In that case, guess I'll have to introduce myself. Hey, {NICKNAME}, I've heard a lot about you. I'm Ifa, a vet from the Flower-Feather Clan.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nice to meet you, bro.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, not you too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh — that wasn't directed at you, Ifa! It's nice to meet you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ororon, Ifa! What brings you to Fontaine?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Huh? How come you're...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm guessing Kinich is here because of that international smuggling case, right? I've heard quite a bit about that.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Word sure gets around quickly, huh.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Haha, first time abroad and you're already making headlines.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Oh, stop it. It's not like I was the center of attention.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: #Wasn't expecting to see {NICKNAME} and Paimon here, too, though.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: C'mon, Ifa.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: A "Traveler," by definition, is someone who travels around.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: ...Fair point.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Back when we first met Cacucu in the wild and I begged you to take him under your wing, I never imagined you'd end up spoiling him rotten.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Heh, and I never imagined you'd be nagging me about it.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Oh, well I definitely saw that coming.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: You're only five years old, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: There are strange sounds coming from Monsieur Neuvillette's office... Do you think we should go in and check on him?

dialogues.speaker: Cornelia
dialogues.text: Nothing new there. The first few days of every month are always noisy.

dialogues.speaker: Eunomia
dialogues.text: What's all that commotion? Are they arguing in there?

dialogues.speaker: Cornelia
dialogues.text: Nothing new there. The first few days of every month are always noisy.

dialogues.speaker: Eunomia
dialogues.text: What's all that commotion? Are they arguing in there?

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: There are strange sounds coming from Monsieur Neuvillette's office... Do you think we should go in and check on him?
